kings2.8.p1.b1.text: Arise, you and your household; go and live as a foreigner wherever you can. For the LORD has decreed a seven-year famine, and it has already come to the land.

kings2.8.p1.b2.text: So the woman had proceeded to do as the man of God had instructed. And she and her household lived as foreigners for seven years in the land of the Philistines.

kings2.8.p1.b3.text: At the end of seven years, when the woman returned from the land of the Philistines, she went to the king to appeal for her house and her land.

kings2.8.p2.b1.text: Please relate to me all the great things Elisha has done.

kings2.8.p2.b2.text: My lord the king, this is the woman, and this is the son Elisha restored to life.

kings2.8.p2.b3.text: Restore all that was hers, along with all the proceeds of the field from the day that she left the country until now.

kings2.8.p3.b1.text: Take a gift in your hand, go to meet the man of God, and inquire of the LORD through him, ‘Will I recover from this illness?’

kings2.8.p3.b2.text: So Hazael went to meet Elisha, taking with him a gift of forty camel loads of every good thing from Damascus.

kings2.8.p3.b3.text: Your son Ben-hadad king of Aram has sent me to ask, ‘Will I recover from this illness?’

kings2.8.p3.b4.text: Go and tell him, ‘You will surely recover.’ But the LORD has shown me that in fact he will die.

kings2.8.p4.b1.text: Elisha fixed his gaze steadily on him until Hazael became uncomfortable. Then the man of God began to weep.

kings2.8.p4.b2.text: Because I know the evil you will do to the Israelites, … You will set fire to their fortresses, kill their young men with the sword, dash their little ones to pieces, and rip open their pregnant women.

kings2.8.p4.b3.text: But how could your servant, a mere dog, do such a monstrous thing?

kings2.8.p4.b4.text: The LORD has shown me that you will be king over Aram.

kings2.8.p5.b1.text: He told me that you would surely recover.

kings2.8.p5.b2.text: But the next day Hazael took a thick cloth, dipped it in water, and spread it over the king’s face. So Ben-hadad died, and Hazael reigned in his place.

kings2.8.p5.b3.text: And Jehoram walked in the ways of the kings of Israel, just as the house of Ahab had done. For he married a daughter of Ahab …

kings2.8.p5.b4.text: Yet for the sake of His servant David, the LORD was unwilling to destroy Judah, since He had promised to maintain a lamp for David and his descendants forever.

kings2.8.p6.b1.text: In the days of Jehoram, Edom rebelled against the hand of Judah … So Jehoram crossed over to Zair with all his chariots. When the Edomites surrounded him and his chariot commanders, he rose up and attacked by night. His troops, however, fled to their homes.

kings2.8.p6.b2.text: And Jehoram rested with his fathers … And his son Ahaziah reigned in his place. … His mother’s name was Athaliah, the granddaughter of Omri king of Israel.

kings2.8.p6.b3.text: So King Joram returned to Jezreel to recover from the wounds that the Arameans had inflicted on him at Ramah when he fought against Hazael king of Aram. Then Ahaziah son of Jehoram king of Judah went down to Jezreel to visit Joram son of Ahab, because Joram had been wounded.
